title: Twingo phase 2 cabin: what Renault corrects between 1998 and 2000
author: Caramagnols
excerpt: Phase 2 does not change the Twingo’s interior idea. It makes it calmer, clearer and a little less austere in presentation.
content:
To understand phase 2, one has to open the door. The real changes are not limited to bumpers. They also lie in the way Renault makes the cabin more adult without touching the core of the project.

A rounder dashboard and a calmer car

Renault reworks the interior presentation with a softer dashboard and a less raw atmosphere. The Twingo does not become luxurious, but it feels better settled in the late 1990s.

That evolution matters in use. A familiar, clear car that feels a little less bare often ages better in the eyes of its owners.

Modularity stays at the centre

The essentials are not abandoned. The sliding rear bench, easy access and spatial logic remain at the core of the project. Phase 2 does not erase the original Twingo; it civilises it.

That balance is what makes it attractive today: still very Twingo in spirit, less fragile in presentation.

Interior wear tells the life of the car

On a used phase 2, fabrics, plastics, controls and seats often offer more useful information than the exterior alone. A clean interior inspires more confidence than a simple polish outside.

The cabin is therefore a real reading point. It reveals care, level of use and sometimes the honesty of the whole car.

This note extends the page the Renault Twingo series 1 phase 2. Within the same cluster, the next useful step is Buying a Twingo phase 2: what to check before saying yes.
